verdict.line: You lose extended trades whenever Gnar's E (Hop) is up and his Rage bar is climbing toward Mega; you win the moment his E is on cooldown and you can wall him in.

brief.thesis: Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw, range 1100) and E (Hop, range 475) give him the ranged poke and reset that produce his solo-kill edge in this matchup, but Hop is on a real cooldown (22/19.5/17/14.5/12s) while your W (Dark Procession, 20/18/16/14/12s) and E (Mourning Mist, 12/11/10/9/8s) recharge faster. The entire lane is a timing read on his E, not a damage race.

tell.watch: Gnar's Rage meter and E cooldown

theirWindow.what: He can engage with Q/E, threaten to transform mid-trade, and hop away from your W wall if you commit — hold position and don't feed him a free all-in.

yourWindow.when: He just used E (Hop) to farm or reposition
yourWindow.what: Walk him down immediately: without E he cannot bounce out of your W (Dark Procession) wall or escape your E (Mourning Mist) slow, so land Q (Last Rites) and E for the kill or a forced flash.

powerCurve.note: Boomerang poke plus E-engage solo-kill threat

start.why: 50% win rate over 86 games and the highest pick rate (63.7%) at this start — the flat damage reduction on hit blunts Gnar's Q poke and his hyper-empowered autos while you farm.

boots.why: 51% win rate over 98 games, 74.8% pick — Gnar's kit is auto-attack and on-hit driven (his W empowers autos, Mega E deals area damage you'll be standing in), so flat physical reduction outvalues Swiftness here.

core.why: Core first item in both listed 50% win rate paths; the stat stick plus movement speed lets you stick through his E hops instead of getting kited.
Second item in every listed build path — the armor shred compounds with your E's own armor reduction, letting your Q procs hit harder once he's marked.
100% win rate over 3 games on this exact Trinity Force into Black Cleaver path — ability haste shortens your W/E cooldowns further, tightening the window where you out-rotate his Hop.

situational.when: gnar's team builds around his on-hit hyper steroid and other auto-reliant damage
lane stabilizes and you're using your ultimate to threaten side lanes instead of fighting him directly
he or his team stack armor to blunt your Q and Black Cleaver shred
you're ahead and want a burst spike to punish his low mobility while Mega Gnar's E is down

runes.keystoneWhy: The 57.7% win rate page built around it is the top-performing option listed; Conqueror ramps through the extended short-range trades this lane forces once you've closed the gap with Hop on cooldown, and it converts into healing for the sustained fights your Q/E combo creates.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 56.2% of games at a 50.6% win rate — Teleport lets you reset after losing early poke exchanges and still answer his roam threat. Flash+Ignite (50%, 33.6% pick) is the alternative if you're confident you can punish his E cooldown with a kill pre-6.

playing.title: Track his Rage bar constantly
playing.detail: Gnar's passive builds Rage in every combat exchange; once it's near max his next ability transforms him into Mega Gnar, swapping his W into an AoE stun and his E into an area slam instead of a jump.

playing.title: Dive the instant his E lands
playing.detail: Per the measured matchup read, Gnar can use E (Hop) to escape your W (Dark Procession) wall — so don't commit the wall as a kill tool until his E is already spent on farming or repositioning.

playing.title: Dodge the boomerang while you farm
playing.detail: His Q (range 1100) is his main poke tool and slows on hit; use your own E (Mourning Mist, range 700) to farm through minion waves and mark him from a safer distance.

playing.title: Dig graves off marked casters
playing.detail: Land Q (Last Rites) on minions he's poking so you heal and build grave count for Mist Walkers without needing to trade autos in his Q range.

playing.title: Respect the Mega Gnar stun window
playing.detail: Once transformed, his W (Wallop) becomes a ground-slam stun instead of a movement steroid — don't walk into melee range during a visible Rage spike.

playing.title: Hold wall for his engage, not his exit
playing.detail: W (Dark Procession) is best placed to block Gnar's approach or cut him off from allies; relying on it to trap a retreating Gnar fails once his E is up again.

playing.title: Pivot to Maiden split-push after level 11
playing.detail: Once Trinity Force and Black Cleaver are online, your R (Eulogy of the Isles, 160/130/100/100/100s cooldown) threatens side waves harder than Gnar can contest — win the lane by out-split-pushing, not out-skirmishing.

brief.patchCaveat: The win rates, pick rates, item paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch (50% over 110 head-to-head games, even lane shape). The mechanical reasoning — the E-cooldown windows, the Rage-bar tells, and the wall-timing read — is my own analysis of why those numbers land where they do.

stats.opponentTip: Keep in mind Gnar can use (E) to escape [W]. Avoid his (Q) while using [E] to farm and kill him when (E) is on cooldown.
